newsitem.title: UK: Windsors' treasures go on show ahead of U.S. sale.
newsitem.headline: Windsors' treasures go on show ahead of U.S. sale.

text.p: Treasures from the French hideaway home of the Duke and Duchess of Windsor went on view in Britain on Sunday ahead of a "royal sale of the century" to be held in New York next month.
The highlight is the mahogany desk at which the duke, as King Edward VIII, signed the instruction of abdication in 1936, giving up the British throne to marry American divorcee Wallis Simpson.

"It is the greatest sale of royal possessions we can remember, and certainly for hundreds of years," said Joseph Friedman of Sotheby's auction house. "The whole comprises a terribly important historical collection."
The lots -- from clocks to coins, medals to trophies, paintings to private papers -- are expected to fetch about 40 million pounds ($64 million) for charity.
The couple spent most of their lives in exile after Edward abdicated in 1936 so that he could marry Mrs Simpson despite bitter opposition from the British establishment.

In 1952 they moved into a luxurious mansion in the Bois de Boulogne suburb close to Paris, where they accumulated a vast collection of artefacts, hired an entourage of servants and maintained a regal lifestyle.

Personal keepsakes in the sale include a private and unofficial diary of the then Prince of Wales's tour to Australia, New Zealand and colonies in the Atlantic and Pacific in 1920, and a map showing his world travels.
On sale will also be some of the couple's stylish clothes, which made them acknowledged fashion icons of the day.
He popularised Fair Isle sweaters and flat Tweed caps and invented the Windsor knot as the perfect finish for a necktie.
She favoured couture by Givenchy, Dior, Yves Saint Laurent, Chanel, Schiaparelli and Madame Gres.
"Together they were the most fashionable couple of the 20th century," said Kerry Taylor, Sotheby's London director of costumes and textiles.
A total of 44,000 objects will go on sale in New York from September 11-19. Four exhibitions of some of the lots will first be staged in Chicago, Los Angeles, Sao Paulo and Buenos Aires.
